title: An algebraically closed family of informational n-qubit purity invariants
authors: Markus Frembs, Giovanni Natale, Christopher S. P. Wever, Philipp A. Hoehn
abstract: We present a family of quadratics in Pauli expectation values, and prove that they constitute state-independent invariants for all n-qubit pure states. This family generalises the two-qubit `pentagon identities', discovered in the reconstruction programme of [P. A. Höhn, Quantum 1, 38 (2017), P. A. Höhn and C. S. P. Wever, Phys. Rev. A 95, 012102 (2017)], where they characterise the space of pure states, as well as the unitary group, and are interpreted as complementarity equalities in the Brukner-Zeilinger information measure. The generalisation to arbitrarily many qubits is nontrivial as it requires new tools which in turn reveal novel structural properties that are absent in the two-qubit case. A thorough analysis of these properties, and their relation with mutual unbiasedness and complementarity in the n-qubit Pauli group, can be found in two companion papers.
summary: This paper develops a generalized theory for finding purity invariants characterizing $n$-qubit pure states, extending concepts from two qubits. It achieves this by defining specific sets within the Pauli group based on maximal complementarity structures rather than just anti-commuting operators. The result provides a systematic classification and enumeration of these fundamental quantum state constraints.
main_problem: The authors aim to find a general family of state-independent invariants for $n$-qubit pure states that successfully generalizes the known 'pentagon identities' from the two-qubit case.
main_result: They introduce a new family of quadratic invariants derived from maximal complementarity structures within the Pauli group, proving these sets constitute purity invariants for arbitrary $n$. The number of such distinct invariants is systematically counted.
method: The analysis employs advanced algebraic techniques involving the structure of Pauli expectation values and identifying specific structured subsets ($J$) of the Pauli group based on commuting/anti-commuting generators.
model_or_system: The system under study consists of $n$-qubit quantum states, whose geometry is characterized by the pure state manifold $	ext{CP}^{2^n-1}$. The diagnostics are built upon the Pauli group $	ilde{\mathbb{P}}_n$ and the Brukner-Zeilinger information measure.
key_observables: The primary observable is the purity invariant $I_\psi(S)$, which must remain constant for all pure states $\psi$. Other key elements include the expectation values of Pauli operators ($\alpha_P$).
important_parameters: The number of qubits, $n$, is the main parameter governing complexity; results are explicitly derived and compared for $n=2$ and $n>2$.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on specific algebraic closure relations concerning sets defined by maximal Abelian subgroups within the Pauli group structure.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates a Venn diagram detailing the set structure defining the invariant set $J$; later sections contain large tables explicitly listing the 28 distinct Pauli string sets for the $n=3$ case.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the need for generalization beyond simple anti-commutation rules (failure at $n>2$). It then defines the invariant set $J$ based on complementarity structures, proves its invariance property using algebraic tools, and finally enumerates and catalogs these invariants for small systems like $n=3$.
why_interesting: This work provides deep structural insights into the geometry of high-dimensional quantum state spaces by identifying conserved quantities (invariants) that are fundamentally linked to the underlying symmetry group structure ($	ext{PSU}(2^n)$).
